items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: I would venture a guess that Al Jolson really came out of a minstrel show... to me, he reminded me of those blackface comedians that I saw as a kid.

ctx.x: And on TOBA, all the black comics wore blackface. Oh yeah, all of the black comics wore blackface, you know. Your makeup was -- whatever the stuff was called, cork. You know, it was cork, and you used greasepaint, make your lips white, you know, white greasepaint. Oh yeah, I used to make myself up. You made up with your hands. That's the way you did it.

But those minstrel shows were really fantastic. Some good performers came out of them. As a matter of fact, I would venture a guess that Al Jolson really came out of a minstrel show; I bet he did come out of a minstrel show. If
you looked it up and tried to find out, because he was, you know, he was singing "Mammy" and all that, and to me, he reminded me of those blackface comedians that I saw as a kid. You know?
